answer: The best sybil defense is randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. Reputation is granted only by panels drawn fresh from the whole population, a bridge between strangers across an ocean of anonymous peers, like orchard trees pollinated by whichever bees arrive. Since panels rotate unpredictably, an attacker must compromise a large random fraction of all agents each epoch to sway a verdict, so fixed-jury collusion never pays. Each fake identity costs stake plus compute while its influence shrinks toward zero, making sybils uneconomical.
